category: premium file host (one-click hoster) selling daily traffic

free_tier.stated: Downloading is free and needs no account: 'Direct Links - Share a single link - no account required for whoever downloads it' and 'Unlimited Downloads - No caps on how many times a file can be downloaded'. The free path's speed and waiting time are not stated; only the premium page prints 'Waiting time 0 seconds'.
free_tier.notes: Free downloads exist and are uncounted by download count. What the free path costs is time, not bytes, and the site does not quantify it.

per_object_cap.stated: Premium prints 'Max file size: Unlimited'; Premium Pro repeats 'Unlimited file size'. No free-tier per-file cap is stated.
per_object_cap.notes: 'Unlimited' is the vendor's word for the paid path; it is recorded as stated, not as measured.

retention.stated: Not stated on the pages read.

egress.terms: Paid traffic is counted per day: Premium carries '50 GB Traffic per day', Premium Pro '200 GB Traffic per day'. Within the allowance: 'High download speed', 'Unlimited parallel downloads', 'Download-Accelerators support'.
egress.free_allowance: 50 GB/day on Premium; 200 GB/day on Premium Pro
egress.price_per_tb: USD 7.22 per TB at the 365-day rate (computed: USD 129.95 / 12 months over 1.5 TB per month)

interface_detail: 'Download-Accelerators support' and 'Unlimited parallel downloads' on the paid tier; multi-thread clients are the intended path. No API is advertised.
tooling: Download managers (IDM, JDownloader class) as named by 'Download-Accelerators support'. A premium key can be activated on the account page, which is the resale surface this corpus checks elsewhere.
chaining: A host that a debrid broker resolves, priced here as the alternative to one: 50 GB a day for USD 34.95 a month is 45 times the traffic of a FilesMonster 30-day pass for twice the price, and both are far above a multi-host debrid subscription.

limits.value: 50 GB per day (Premium), 200 GB per day (Premium Pro), reset daily
uploading requires Partner status, 'granted after a review'

limits_note: The traffic counter starts 'From 50 GB' and does not accumulate: a day unused is a day lost. The write gate is separate and only affects publishing, not retrieval.
binding_note: At 1 TiB a month (about 34 GB a day) the 50 GB daily bucket on Premium is enough, so the binding constraint becomes the monthly bill rather than a technical wall; at 1 TiB a day only Premium Pro's 200 GB would still fall short by a factor of five.

identity_cost.detail: Buying premium needs a card: 'Card, crypto and more' on the checkout. Downloading needs nothing at all, and a prepaid premium key can be activated without a card ('If you already have a premium key, you can activate it on the My Profile page').

reliability_note: Publishing is closed to new accounts: 'Not every account can upload files - Partner status is granted after a review'. That keeps the catalogue curated and also means a client cannot use this host as free storage, only as a retrieval target.
confidence_note: Free-download terms, the two daily buckets and all four prices were read on the vendor's pages. The free path's actual speed and wait are unstated by the vendor and were not measured.

evidence.proved: the prices (30 days USD 34.95, 60 days USD 49.95, 90 days USD 61.95, 365 days USD 129.95) and the buckets ('50 GB Traffic per day' Premium, '200 GB Traffic per day' Premium Pro)
'Unlimited Downloads - No caps on how many times a file can be downloaded', 'Direct Links ... no account required for whoever downloads it', and the Partner-only upload gate
two sale models exist (purchase-only, and premium-or-purchase), which is how a single file can be priced above the subscription

price_per_tb_month: USD 23.30 per TB-month on a 30-day pass; USD 7.22 per TB-month at the annual rate
notes: The record exists for the daily-bucket comparison: it is the only host in this set that sells traffic by the day with no rollover, which is the shape a downloader with bursty demand wants and a steady one does not.

extras.bucket_math: 50 GB/day is 1.5 TB a 30-day month; 200 GB/day is 6 TB. The annual pass at USD 129.95 over 18.25 TB is the cheapest per byte here
